# support-ops-knowledge-qa

Customer support operations analytics in plain Python (standard library only, pytest for tests).

**All data is synthetic.** Tickets, help-center articles, macros, agents and QA reviews are generated by a seeded script (`supportops/synth.py`). Nothing is connected to Zendesk, Intercom, or any helpdesk, and no real customers, companies or people appear. Numbers in the report describe the generated data, not any real operation; where the generator and an analyzer share vocabulary the scores are optimistic and the report says so.

## What it does

| Module | Question it answers |
|---|---|
| `kb.py` | Which ticket topics have no article, a stale article (>180 days), or an article that does not match what customers write? How many tickets could a good article deflect? (deflect rate is an explicit 25% assumption) |
| `trends.py` | Weekly CSAT / first-response / resolution; daily anomaly flags using a trailing-window robust z-score (median/MAD) |
| `qa.py` | Weighted rubric scorecards per agent, plus calibration: criterion SD across reviewers, agreement within one point, reviewer severity bias |
| `macros.py` | Suggest canned responses for ticket text (TF-IDF cosine, abstains on vague text), with top-1/top-3 evaluation |
| `forecast.py` | Arrivals by weekday x hour, Erlang C staffing for an SLA (80% first response in 30 min), shrinkage, and a fluid backlog projection against a roster |
| `voc.py` | Keyword themes, CSAT by theme, terms over-represented in 1-2 star replies. No LLM |

## Run

```
python3 -m supportops all     # regenerate data/synthetic.json and report/index.html
python3 -m pytest -q
open report/index.html        # static, no JS, no network
```

## Injected events (so detectors can be checked)

The generator injects two known events: a staffing gap (first response x3.2) on day 40 and a billing incident (extra volume, slow replies, low CSAT on billing tickets) on day 60. The tests assert the anomaly detector flags them, that three topics with no article are reported as gaps, and that the QA calibration finds the seeded reviewer bias and the noisiest criterion.

## Limits

- Topic tagging is keyword rules; real queues need better taxonomy.
- Forecast is a weekday-hour mean: no trend, seasonality, or incident modeling. Roster and shrinkage are invented parameters.
- Macro accuracy and VOC lifts are measured on text written from small templates; expect lower on real tickets.
